title: The Iran War Sent Shock Waves Through Asia That Are Likely to Spread
partialText: The Asia-Pacific was hit hard and quick by the war in Iran and its energy bottlenecks. Scenes of crisis there indicate that problems are multiplying and spreading.

title: Vance Heads to New Talks With Iran. At Stake: Peace and His Own Standing.
partialText: The vice president is again center stage, after abruptly leaving the first round of high-level Iranian peace talks without an agreement.

title: Strait of Hormuz Traffic Is at a Standstill Again
partialText: Few vessels are crossing after Iran reversed course on reopening the vital waterway and ships came under attack.

title: U.S. Attacks and Seizes Cargo Ship Near Iran, and a First Step Toward Tariff Refunds
partialText: Plus, Lego crime.

title: Trump Administration to Begin Refunding $166 Billion in Tariffs
partialText: The government will debut a system to repay importers two months after the Supreme Court struck down tariffs at the heart of the president’s trade policy.

title: Why Your Paycheck Feels Smaller
partialText: Ben Casselman, our chief economics correspondent, explains why wages are not keeping up with inflation and what that means for American workers and the economy.

title: Why Gas Prices Go Up Fast and Take So Long to Fall
partialText: Fuel station owners take some of the hit for consumers when oil prices surge. On the way down, they try to get their money back.

title: Epstein Wanted Connections at Harvard. Files Show Many Faculty Members Were Happy to Help.
partialText: New documents reveal what professors did to help Jeffrey Epstein get inside Harvard’s gates.

title: Starmer Tells Parliament He Was Kept in the Dark on Mandelson Vetting
partialText: Prime Minister Keir Starmer addressed British lawmakers on Monday after it emerged that Peter Mandelson, his onetime ambassador to the United States, was rejected for top security clearances.

title: Ukraine, Short on Troops, Is Turning to Robots to Help Its War Efforts
partialText: Ukraine is using unmanned ground vehicles armed with bombs, guns or rockets to carry out attacks and keep its soldiers out of harm’s way.

title: The President Is Coming to the White House Correspondent’s Dinner
partialText: A president who relishes attacking the news media is set to break his boycott of an event celebrating the news media. What could go wrong?

title: Why a Democratic Senate, Once Unthinkable, Is a Real Possibility
partialText: Helped by a favorable national environment and strong candidate recruitment, Democrats are tied or ahead in four Republican-held seats, polls show.

title: Big Names Wait in the Wings as Virginians Decide Their House Maps
partialText: With Virginians voting Tuesday to accept or reject redistricting, candidates from both parties await the voters’ judgment to decide whether — or where — to run for Congress.

title: A Leaner Saudi Arabia Turns From Grandiose Plans to Pragmatism
partialText: A decade after Mohammed bin Salman unveiled his “Vision 2030” program to transform the country’s economy, the kingdom is facing financial strains and reassessing its trajectory.

title: Influencers Are Spinning Nicotine as a ‘Natural’ Health Hack
partialText: The influencers, many of them aligned with the Make America Healthy Again Movement, say the medical establishment has unfairly demonized the compound.

title: Northeast Swings From 90 Degrees to Freezing Cold in Just a Few Days
partialText: Central Park and other spots around the region set record-high temperatures last week. Freeze watches were in place on Monday. What’s going on?

title: Javier Milei Tamed Argentina’s Inflation. Now He Wants to Reshape Its Values.
partialText: Argentina’s right-wing president has tamed the country’s runaway inflation. Now he wants to transform its values.

title: Haunted by ‘Dark Thoughts,’ Louisiana Father Kills 8 Children
partialText: Seven of the eight children killed were the shooter’s own. Relatives said the gunman, who died in a confrontation with the police, was struggling with mental health problems and stressed about his relationship with his wife.

title: C.E.O.s Are the Heads of Companies. Should They Also Be the Face?
partialText: Most chief executives are not recognizable to their customers. But when they step into the limelight, the rewards — and the risks — can be great.

title: The Town That Reveals All of Trump’s Bad Economic Ideas
partialText: The jobs are coming back, despite President Trump’s tariffs and harsh immigration enforcement.

title: Does the Trump Administration Really Want More Teen Pregnancies?
partialText: The new Title X guidance from the Trump administration mentions contraception only once.

title: A Supreme Court Scoop
partialText: We go behind the scenes at the nation’s highest court.

title: Justices to Hear Case on Catholic Preschools That Reject Children of Gay Parents
partialText: Catholic preschools in Colorado that decline to enroll families with L.G.B.T.Q. children or parents sued to participate in a state-funded program.

title: A Decisive Win Raises Bulgarians’ Hopes for Change
partialText: An election victory by a former president, Rumen Radev, gives the country a chance for stability and to clean out the corruption that has stymied its growth.

title: Tsunami Warnings Downgraded in Japan After Strong Offshore Earthquake
partialText: The 7.7-magnitude undersea quake occurred off Iwate Prefecture, on the northeastern coast of Japan’s main island, Honshu.

title: Stolen Letters That John Keats Sent to His Beloved Are Found
partialText: The eight letters by the 19th-century Romantic poet to his fiancée, Fanny Brawne, were taken decades ago from a Whitney family estate on Long Island.
